summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for evaluation of a persistent headache lasting three weeks, associated with photophobia, phonophobia, nausea, and transient visual disturbances. A non-contrast head CT showed no acute intracranial pathology, supporting a diagnosis of migraine rather than structural or infectious causes. She was unable to take her usual migraine medication, Imitrex, due to interactions with her HIV regimen. During the admission, she was treated for an asymptomatic urinary tract infection with ciprofloxacin and started on lisinopril for newly detected hypertension. Her HIV remained well controlled, and other chronic conditions were managed without change. She was discharged home in good condition with instructions to follow up with her primary care provider and neurology for ongoing headache management.
